headline: Check Firefly Lottery and Flood Stage Alerts
reservation: Congaree does not require a general entry fee or reservation, but the synchronous firefly viewing in late spring requires a specific lottery-based vehicle pass. Camping at Longleaf or Bluff sites must be reserved through Recreation.gov; there are no walk-in accommodations within the park. Always check the official NPS 'Current Conditions' for boardwalk closures due to river flooding.

days.title: Old-Growth Boardwalks

stops.name: Harry Hampton Visitor Center
stops.detail: Begin with the park film and check the 'mosquito meter' to gauge current insect activity levels.

stops.name: Boardwalk Loop Trail
stops.detail: Walk the 2.4-mile elevated path to see champion loblolly pines and the knees of ancient cypress trees.

days.driving: Allow 45–60 minutes from Columbia; roads are flat and rural.
days.note: Boardwalk sections can be extremely slippery when wet or covered in fine silt after flooding.

days.title: Canoe Trails and Deep Forest

stops.name: Cedar Creek Canoe Trail
stops.detail: Paddle through the blackwater creek to see the forest from a water-level perspective; check for downed trees.

stops.name: Weston Lake Overlook
stops.detail: Pause at this former river channel to look for turtles and wading birds in the quiet waters.

days.driving: Local transfers are minimal; allow time for equipment unloading at the landing.
days.note: Paddling requires independent equipment or a pre-booked private outfitter; the park does not rent boats.

days.title: Regional Heritage and Columbia

stops.name: Bates Ferry Trail
stops.detail: Follow this historic road trace to the Congaree River, focusing on the cultural history of the ferry crossing.

stops.name: South Carolina State Museum
stops.detail: Head into Columbia to explore regional natural history and indoor exhibits if the afternoon humidity rises.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for transit between the park and the state capital.
days.note: The Bates Ferry area is prone to flooding; check river gauges on the NPS website.

intel.title: Visitor Center Hub
intel.text: The main parking lot at Harry Hampton serves the boardwalk and fills quickly during the spring firefly season. Overflow parking is limited and may require a significant walk to the trailhead.

intel.title: Floodplain Dead Zones
intel.text: Cellular reception is mostly absent once you descend from the visitor center into the bottomland forest. Carry a physical map or use GPS-only apps for the backcountry trails.

intel.title: Gadsden and Hopkins Services
intel.text: There are no gas stations or food services inside the park. Hopkins and Gadsden offer basic fuel, but major shopping should be completed in Columbia.

intel.title: Optimal Seasonality
intel.text: Mid-week visits in November provide peak foliage without the weekend crowds. Summer visits should be limited to early mornings to avoid the 90+ degree humidity.

intel.title: Water Level Access
intel.text: The park is a natural floodplain; heavy rain in the Blue Ridge Mountains can flood the boardwalk days later. Check the official NPS flood alerts before leaving Columbia.

plan.arrival: Fly into CAE and rent a car. Stop in Columbia for a cooler, water, and heavy-duty insect repellent before driving to Hopkins for check-in.
plan.vehicle: Any standard vehicle is suitable for the paved access roads; high-clearance is not required for the main trailheads.
plan.goldenHour: Weston Lake offers beautiful reflections at sunset, though the forest canopy makes the 'hour' feel much shorter than in open areas.
